newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends strong on cold weather, oil down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends strong on cold weather, oil down.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed higher on Wednesday as temperatures dropped in key U.S. livestock areas, increasing demand for high-protein feed, traders said.
Soyoil prices tumbled on talk of heavy deliveries against the January contract and on commercial selling tied to falling crush margins.

Forecasts called for temperatures to drop to minus 10 to minus 20 degrees Farenheit in the western Corn Belt on Friday. Temperatures were expected to remain below normal through the weekend, meteorologists said.
Crush margins slipped on Wednesday which encouraged crushers to buy soybeans and sell the finished products, traders said.
CBOT reported January crush margins down 4.15 cents per bushel to 54.21 and March margins down 1.02 cents at 43.53.
Traders also noted registration of soyoil in deliverable locations rose by 60 lots to 4,858 lots on Wednesday, prompting talk of heavy deliveries against the January.
Soymeal closed $1.00 to $4.00 per ton higher with March up $4.00 at $234.80. Soyoil finished 0.10 to 0.14 cent per lb lower with March down 0.12 at 24.77.
Cargill reportedly bought 150 lots March soymeal and was also said to be a buyer of the May and July. ADM was a small-lot buyer of the March and July, traders said.
Both Cargill and ADM were sellers of soyoil and Produce Grain sold at least 150 lots March, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 23,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 22,684 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 25,000 lots, against Tuesday's actual volume of 25,379 lots.
